candidates.why: bit_write_TU loops bit_write_RS(dat, chain[i]) at 2150; bit_write_RS->bit_write_RC->bit_chain_alloc does realloc(dat->chain) at 3015, which can free the old buffer. If the caller's `chain` aliases dat->chain (writing a string stored in the same chain), chain[i] at 2150 is a use-after-free. No guard/refresh of `chain` after the realloc.

Same pattern as bit_write_TU: loop at 2166 calls bit_write_RS(dat, chain[i]) after bit_write_RS(dat, length) at 2164; the realloc at 3015 inside bit_write_RC can invalidate `chain` if it aliases dat->chain.
Loop at 2182 calls bit_write_RS(dat, chain[i]) after bit_write_RL at 2180; realloc at 3015 can free the buffer `chain` points into if it aliases dat->chain, leaving chain[i] dangling.

Loop at 2209 calls bit_write_RL(dat, chain[i]) after bit_write_RL at 2207; bit_write_RL also goes through bit_write_RC/bit_chain_alloc (realloc at 3015), so `chain` can be freed mid-loop if it aliases dat->chain.

In the else branch, loop at 1520 calls bit_write_RC(dat, chain[i]); bit_write_RC may call bit_chain_alloc -> realloc(dat->chain) at 3015. If `chain` points into dat->chain (e.g. copying within the same chain), chain[i] is used after the buffer was freed.

Loop at 1823 calls bit_write_RC(dat, chain[i]) after bit_write_BS at 1821; realloc at 3015 inside bit_write_RC can free the buffer `chain` refers to if it aliases dat->chain, making chain[i] a use-after-free.

bit_chain_alloc at 3993 is done once before the loop, but the loop at 3995-3996 calls bit_write_RS per element, each of which can trigger another realloc at bits.c:3015. `dest` itself is heap (not dat->chain) so it survives, but the loop is unguarded against further chain growth; flagged as suspicious for the aliasing/overflow pattern.

Loop at 4008-4009 calls bit_write_RS(dat, *s++) after a single bit_chain_alloc at 4006; subsequent reallocs at bits.c:3015 inside bit_write_RC are not accounted for, and `s` is a raw pointer into a struct field that is not refreshed.

bit_write_RS at 4510/4539 can realloc dat->chain (bits.c:3015); then rbuf->value.str.u.data is passed to bit_write_TF at 4542. If that data aliases dat->chain, it is used after the realloc freed it. Also `new` is used at 4530 then freed at 4535 (that order is fine), but the chain realloc between 4510 and 4530 is unguarded.
